title: Fatal-error handling becomes a no-op once a graceful shutdown has started, leaving the process half torn down
test: tests/serverIntegration.test.js: 'a fatal error during a graceful shutdown still ends the process with a failure code'; unit tests in tests/shutdownCoordinator.test.js (16 cases: clean graceful path exits 0, force-exit timer armed before the first await, fatal mid-graceful exits 1, fatal after the graceful cleanup exits 1 and cleans up again, graceful shutdown throwing before cleanup exits 1, cleanup or listener close throwing exits 1, exit funnel runs once and a fatal phase never exits 0)
proof: On the unchanged server the integration test starts the real server, connects a Socket.IO client, then POSTs /api/test/shutdown and, on the same kept-alive connection a few milliseconds later (inside the 150 ms room-ended flush), POSTs /api/test/unhandled-rejection. The log shows '[fatal] shutdownReason=unhandled-rejection: Error: injected unhandled rejection' and nothing else: requestFatalShutdown returned at once because isShuttingDown was already true, no cleanup and no exit(1) followed. The graceful path then finished on its own and the process exited with code 0 ('0 !== 1', expected 1; 6.9 s in the last run because the open client held the listener until the 5 s force timer). After the change the same test passes: the client got room-ended 'server-shutdown' first, the fatal error cleaned up and exited 1 at once with '[fatal] exiting after unhandled-rejection; an external supervisor must restart Nextra.' (six reruns, all passing). The shutdown-throws-before-cleanup case and the timer order cannot be driven in the real server (no seam makes the graceful body throw), so the coordinator unit tests cover them with injected exit, cleanup and timer functions.
